tldr: Z.ai (Zhipu) released GLM-5.4 on Nov 23, a 750B loop transformer that passes its 28 weight-shared layers twice instead of stacking more unique layers. It is the lab's first looped flagship, pitched at generalized coding, and launched without open weights.
whats_new: Zhipu now claims the 750B GLM-5.4 matches 2-3T-class models, but that claim comes from Chinese financial press and has no independent benchmark behind it yet.
why_it_matters: Looping shared layers trades parameter count for repeated compute per token, so GLM-5.4's memory footprint and its latency and cost per token may not scale the way a plain 750B model's would.

status.detail: The model is announced and described, but open weights and independent evaluations are both still missing.

beats.headline: GLM-5.4 ships as a 750B loop transformer that runs 28 layers twice
beats.summary: Z.ai frames it as its first looped model, aimed at generalized coding.

beats.headline: Zhipu claims 2-3T-class performance from a 750B base
beats.summary: The headline efficiency claim is reported, not independently verified.

open_questions: Will Z.ai publish GLM-5.4 open weights, and under what license?
Does an independent benchmark confirm 2-3T-class performance from the 750B model?
What do per-token latency and price look like when every token runs the 28 layers twice?
Do other labs adopt looped layers in flagship models after GLM-5.4?
take_for_builders: Do not swap GLM-5.4 into a coding-agent stack on the 2-3T claim; wait for weights or API pricing, then rerun your own coding evals and measure latency per token.
